name: GatewayEVM arbitrary-call USDC allowance drain (Base leg)
summary: The attacker set IsArbitraryCall on GatewayZEVM.call, so ZetaClient zeroed the sender and the TSS signed a destination execute() that routed into _executeArbitraryCall, whose onCall/onRevert-only deny-list let a transferFrom selector through; the Base GatewayEVM proxy then pulled 110,342.28643 USDC from a team wallet's pre-existing gateway allowance to the attacker EOA.
notes: The fifth and final pre-incident Upgraded event selected implementation 0x1fff55ccf855212f6b5530c468b44f9a5246572e, which carries the unrestricted _executeArbitraryCall sink; the next two upgrades (blocks 45438102 and 46522899) are the post-incident patches.

Exact receipt accounting: one USDC Transfer of 110342286430 units from team wallet 0x8f1aa4dc8efdb3faa5060179e90ec3572ff86e38 to attacker EOA 0x00467f5921f1a343b96b9bf71ae7e9054ae72ea4 inside the TSS-signed execute(). This record covers the single largest destination leg only; the wider campaign drained about $333,868 across 9 TSS-signed executes on Ethereum, BSC, Base, and Arbitrum, consolidated to 139.01439 ETH. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas; victim funds moved via pre-existing ERC20 allowance, not from custody inside the gateway.
